body:
cc @graouts @lilles @flackr 

FWIW, not the most familiar with scroll-driven animations, but on the test-case above Gecko and Blink get `100, 0, 0, 150`, and I'm not quite sure why? I guess the ongoing animation (with the unknown timeline) gets canceled and another one doesn't quite start yet?

I guess per the discussion in https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13807 the right behavior in that test-case is 100, 100, 100, 150? `[inactive, inactive, inactive, active timeline]`, rather than the current `[inactive, null|inactive, null, active]` behavior?

The CSS Working Group just discussed `[scroll-animations-1] When exactly does the timeline change take effect? What does the initial scroll snapshot look like?`.
The full IRC log of that discussion <emilio> dshin-moz: we're implementing scroll-linked animations and there are some WebKit / Blink impl differences
<emilio> ... when a timeline starts being applied
<flackr> q+
<emilio> ... webkit seems to think the effect shouldn't take effect immediately and Blink does
<emilio> ... there's multiple things could be going on, like scroll snapshots being 0
<astearns> ack flackr
<emilio> ... but wanted to figure out how to align on this
<emilio> flackr: the spec is clear that a change of timeline happens immediately
<emilio> ... the caveat is that scroll timelines will not update multiple times if they're invalidated during a frame
<emilio> ... I haven't looked at the particular test-case but changing the timeline itself should take immediate effect
<emilio> ... I don't think anything in the spec that says otherwise
<emilio> q+
<emilio> graouts: I'm here and I don't disagree with that assertion
<bramus> scribe+
<dshin-moz> q+
<bramus> emilio: other question is, when you get the scrolltimeline, the offset can be multiple things. some of them can be cyclic. thats why you’d want to update multiple times
<bramus> … dont think blink is updating right aaway?
<emilio> flackr: Blink does a pass after ResizeObserver processing
<emilio> ... e.g. if you create a scroll timeline without layout information we detect that and at the end of the frame we update it
<bramus> emilio: right, that’s the post-layout stuff in the HTML spec.
<emilio> s/spec/spec PR/
<astearns> ack emilio
<bramus> … so you mention that, if there is no layout info at the time you switch, then at the end of the frame we update
<bramus> … but unclear to me what happens
<bramus> … does it matter if you call getBoundingClientRect before style change for example?
<bramus> … before siwthcing timelines … would be broken
<bramus> flackr: something being a scroller depends on style
<bramus> emilio: but the scrolloffset
<bramus> flackr: is not necesariily known
<bramus> … after style and layout, we check if that has changed
<bramus> emilio: but _since when_? that I’d like to know
<bramus> … does the animation timeline start off at the previous value or at 0 and then goes through post layout stuff?
<bramus> flackr: the state at the start of the timeline, if the TL existed before you set it, it woul dhave a previous snasphot state
<bramus> emilio: so if the TL is created there is no snapshot
<bramus> … makes sense
<bramus> … only 1 place where you update scrolltimlines in aframe
<bramus> … seems sensible
<bramus> flackr: yep
<bramus> emilio: So the webkit behavior is unintentional, because even within the same frame ??? like you do multiple style updates
<bramus> … so we are confused by a webkit bug and unobvious/unspecced behavior
<astearns> ack dshin-moz
<emilio> dshin-moz: just wanted to clarify, if the update is immediate, if authors wanted to change the scroller they're referring to, they might see a brief flash of no animation-styled element
<emilio> flackr: no
<emilio> flackr: if the timeline existed they'd have a time already
<emilio> ... if the timeline was new, after style and layout we'd detect it and re-run style and layout
<emilio> ... so initially it'd have a time of 0
<emilio> ... but before a visible frame it'd get a value like e.g. resizeobserver
<emilio> astearns: do we need any spec clarifications about when timelines are created and how they get updated
<emilio> flackr: I'd suggest Emilio or David to send PRs if there are improvements to be made
<emilio> ... would be happy to review
<bramus> emilio: big thing is mainly unblocking that html spec pr work, which got a bit stalled
<bramus> … needs to hook into this whole system
<bramus> … seems like there are some broken WPTs that also confuse us
<bramus> … fixing those should be uncontroversial ideally
<emilio> astearns: cool, so should we take it back to the issue and fix tests etc, then go back to the spec if there are test updates not supported by the spec?
<emilio> emilio: dshin-moz: sg
